content.tagline: Pianist | Performer on Historical Keyboard Instruments
content.intro: Victoria Chikalkina is a pianist with a broad creative range whose performing career harmoniously combines a deep command of the academic piano repertoire with a commitment to historically informed performance (HIP). Her artistry is distinguished by impeccable pianism, attention to musical rhetoric, subtleties of articulation, and the revelation of each instrument's unique sonic qualities.

sections.title: Academic Piano Foundation and the Modern Grand Piano
paragraphs: Classical piano art occupies a central place in the artist's career. The foundation of her professional training was her studies at the Moscow State Tchaikovsky Conservatory, which she graduated from with honours in 2023 in the class of Professor Maxim Philippov.

In the same year, she was awarded the prestigious Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship (ESKAS) to continue her piano studies at the Geneva Haute École de Musique under Paul Kock and Fabrizio Chiovetta.
sections.listIntro: Victoria's outstanding mastery on the modern piano and in chamber ensembles has been recognised with numerous awards at major Russian and European competitions:
items: Rachmaninoff Days in Moscow — First Prize (Piano and Chamber Ensemble categories, 2015)
I Independent Piano Competition — First Prize (Moscow, 2019)
Val-de-Travers International Piano Competition — Audience Prize (Switzerland, 2021)
Lavaux Classic Piano Competition — Third Prize (Cully, 2024)
sections.closing: Her pianistic school was greatly shaped by masterclasses with such distinguished artists as Rena Shereshevskaya, Alexander Kobrin, Laurent Cabasso, Ricardo Castro, Jean-Claude Vanden Eynden, Elena Kuznetsova, Vera Nosina, Eduardo Delgado, and François Dumont.

sections.title: Immersion in Historical Keyboards (from 2025)
paragraphs: From 2025, Victoria Chikalkina opened a new and important chapter in her creative life, beginning to specialise in historical keyboard instruments in Geneva. There she enriches her performing experience, refining her mastery of the fortepiano in the class of Pierre Goy and studying the harpsichord with Constance Thiard.
sections.listIntro: Her research and performing interest in authentic sound includes regular work with distinguished historical instruments and replicas by the great makers of the past, including:
items: An instrument by Johann Andreas Stein (1783)

sections.title: Concert Activity
paragraphs: Since 2021, Victoria has been a soloist of the Ryazan Regional Philharmonic. She maintains an active solo and ensemble concert career, performing regularly on international stages.

The pianist takes part in major European musical events, including the Festival de L'Ensemble L'Encyclopédie at the Fondation-Musée Zubov in Geneva, the Sobrio Festival, and the Fête de la Musique in Geneva and Neuchâtel (where she performed in the Franz Liszt Hall and on the stage of the Temple du Bas Neuchâtel). She has also been invited to perform on several occasions at the embassies of Switzerland and Iceland in Moscow.
